criteria.criterion: steward::run invokes an AgentDriver with the stored STEWARD_PROMPT as the system prompt (via the role definition, unchanged in meaning) and records that invocation (role, usage, cost) like other roles' invocations; the call site in note_finished still runs in the background and never blocks the main flow.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. In steward.rs, DriverAgent::survey_in composes only `role.{name}` with role.prompt as the system prompt. It calls self.driver.invoke with Role::Steward and a FileSink for usage. build_invocation_record (now a free function in invocation.rs) builds the Invocation record, and run() commits it under records/steward-runs/. note_finished takes a handle from driver.share() and runs everything inside spawn_background. The integration test checks that the stored prompt reaches the agent, that steward_runs holds the 0.02 cost, and that exactly one Steward call is made at the fifth finished task.

criteria.criterion: The steward's invocation is read-only: its tool policy allows reading the repository snapshot, records, prompts, briefs and git history (git log/show/diff) plus read-only GitHub queries (gh run/pr/api GET for CI, PRs, deploys), and denies writes, pushes, and mutating gh/git commands; policy tests cover both allowed and denied cases.
criteria.evidence: Read in policy.rs. check_gh blocks `-f`/`-F`/`--field`/`--raw-field`/`--input` only when the flag is a word of its own, or a `--name=value` long form. A shorthand with its value attached, such as `-ftitle=x` or `-Fbody=@file`, is treated as a harmless flag. pflag reads it as `-f title=x`, and gh then sends a POST, so `gh api repos/o/r/issues -ftitle=x` is allowed and would create an issue. The steward's environment passes HOME (athena.toml env_pass = ["HOME", "PATH"]), so gh would normally find the user's stored login. The tests cover `-f title=x` only as separate words. Separately, the working directory is a one-commit snapshot, so `git show` and `git diff` cannot reach older commits; history is a log file only, and the docs say so.

criteria.criterion: The agent returns structured output (work items with kind, key, title, rung, source and evidence references, and a request text); Athena validates it, then still routes every item through decide(): rungs at or below the role's limit queue a request via RequestQueue, higher rungs (owner goals, brief requirements, design decisions) queue only a proposal with evidence.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. StewardOutput and StewardItemOutput in outputs.rs have a hardened schema. changes_from_output checks that key, title and request are not empty, that evidence is present, that cited jobs exist in the records, that paths stay inside the repository, and that commits are hex ids, then redacts the free text. run() sends every change through decide() with RequestQueue. The integration test shows a defaults-conventions item queuing a request and a brief-requirements item queuing only a proposal that cites its evidence.

criteria.criterion: Each source the agent reports it could not read (including GitHub when gh or network is unavailable) becomes a blind-spot work item naming that source; items whose key already exists in records are not queued twice.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. Each entry in survey.unread becomes blind_spot(source) with key `blind-spot:{source}`. known_keys is loaded from the records and checked before decide(). The test checks that 'GitHub (gh is not installed)' becomes a blind spot, and that a second run with the same findings queues nothing.

criteria.criterion: The old repeated_failures counting is no longer the steward's only reasoning: it is either removed or provided to the agent as input, and docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md and CHANGELOG.md say the steward now calls a model.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. steward_brief puts the repeated_failures classes into the agent's brief. roles-and-ladder.md says '**The steward now calls a model.**', and CHANGELOG.md begins 'The steward now calls a model.'

findings.summary: The gh policy lets an attached shorthand field through (`gh api <endpoint> -ftitle=x`), which turns the read into a POST that changes GitHub.
findings.evidence: The flag check only matches whole words, or `--name=value` split at '='. The word `-ftitle=x` splits into '-ftitle', which is not in the deny list, and is then skipped as an ordinary flag. pflag reads `-fVALUE` as `-f VALUE`, and gh api switches to POST when any field is given. HOME is passed to the agent (athena.toml env_pass), so gh would normally have the user's login. No test covers the attached form. Fix: deny any word starting with -f or -F (or anything other than known read-only flags), and add tests for `-ftitle=x` and `-Fx=@f`.

findings.summary: The steward cannot run `git show` or `git diff` on older commits; it gets only a 300-commit log file.
findings.evidence: Snapshot::create makes a one-commit copy, and history/log.txt holds only hashes, dates, subjects and trailers. The docs state the limit and why (private paths are hidden), but the request asked for broad read access to git history.

findings.summary: Files changed outside the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: store.rs adds Records::steward_runs, which the change needs. The three test files handle the new Role::Steward. None of the four is on the list.

findings.summary: Blind-spot keys for agent failures include the error text, so the same problem can be queued again with a different key.
findings.evidence: Agent failures are reported as unread `steward-agent: {detail}`, and the key becomes `blind-spot:steward-agent: ...`. Any change in the detail text makes a new key, so the dedup does not catch it.

findings.summary: The steward borrows the verifier's model, budget and timeout.
findings.evidence: model: config.models.verifier and max_budget_usd: config.budget.verifier_usd. This is noted under future work in the docs.

summary: The change does what was asked. The steward is now a model-backed agent. Its stored prompt (still steward-1) is the system prompt. It runs through a shared AgentDriver on the background thread and gets a read-only working directory: the code, prompts, docs, records/ and a 300-commit log, plus `gh` for GitHub. Its typed output is validated and every item goes through decide(). Each unread source becomes a blind-spot item, and keys already in the records are skipped. The invocation is recorded under records/steward-runs/. Docs and CHANGELOG were updated. I ran `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` on the snapshot, and all were clean. The verdict is still fail, because the read-only promise in criterion 2 has a gap. In the new gh policy, `gh api <endpoint> -ftitle=x` gets through: the flag value is attached to `-f` instead of passed as a separate argument. gh treats any field as a reason to send a POST, so the agent could create or change things on GitHub. The steward's environment passes HOME (athena.toml env_pass), so gh would normally find the user's login, which makes the gap reachable. Fixing it, with a test for the attached form, should be a small change. Smaller issues: the agent cannot run `git show` or `git diff` on older commits, only read a log of them; store.rs and three test files changed outside the deliverables list; and blind-spot keys for agent failures include the error text, so they are not stable.
